prediction.likelyOutcome: TWE is likely to recover materially more than ODOT's trial position of roughly $126,250, with a jury verdict most plausibly landing at or somewhat above TWE's admitted $1,003,000 figure (which already reflects remainder damage), given ODOT's own commissioners repeatedly found far higher damages across four reports. The excluded water-damage evidence (worth roughly another $663,400) is the main upside TWE is foreclosed from at trial absent a successful appeal of the exclusion ruling, and TWE's separate counterclaims against ODOT and its insurer face real notice, assignment, and double-recovery defenses that limit their incremental value.

issues.label: Just Compensation — Value of Part Taken and Damages to Remainder

figures.label: ODOT trial appraisal (just compensation, no remainder damage)
figures.quote: just compensation to TWE was no more than approximately $126,250, none of which is attributed to injury to the remainder property

figures.label: TWE expert appraisal at trial (water damage excluded)
figures.quote: it was entitled to $1,003,000, of which approximately $829,500 was due to damage to the remainder property

figures.label: Original Commissioners' Report award
figures.quote: The court-appointed Commissioners assessed compensation due for the property to be taken and damages to the remainder at $847,000. ODOT paid that amount into court.

figures.label: Second Alias Commissioners' Report (exclusive of water-damage negligence claims)
figures.quote: the Commissioners returned their "Second Alias Report" assessing compensation due to TWE, exclusive of damages due to the claimed negligence of third parties, to again be $3,890,000

figures.label: TWE appraiser's diminution value including water damage and secondary effects
figures.quote: if the water damage and its secondary effects (e.g., mold and loss of electrical power for a long period of time) were taken into account, the total decrease in value amounted to approximately $1,666,400

issues.label: TWE's Counterclaims Against ODOT (Inverse Condemnation, Negligence, Trespass, Nuisance, Breach of Contract)

figures.label: Claimed covered loss
figures.quote: claiming TWE had sustained losses covered by insurance of more than $2,663,159

figures.label: Amount UNIC had paid
figures.quote: of which UNIC had paid only $396,093

outcome.description: At the February 2018 trial the Tulsa County jury returned a verdict of $340,000 for TWE (ODOT's evidence: about $126,250; TWE's: $1,003,000), and the court entered judgment for ODOT for $420,000 of withdrawn deposit in excess of the verdict. The Court of Civil Appeals vacated the judgment and remanded on July 23, 2020 (mandate March 2021), holding the exclusion of the water-damage evidence was reversible error.
outcome.finalNote: Vacated and remanded for a new trial; no final figure.
